name: Post-fascism
summary: Post-fascism describes parties that grew out of fascist or neo-fascist movements and now work within electoral democracy, dropping totalitarian methods, paramilitary violence and corporatist economics while keeping ultranationalism, anti-communism, traditional family values, tough security and hostility to immigration and to liberal universalism. Scholars such as Griffin see it as a modernised nationalist rebirth project; Tamás stresses that it fits easily into global capitalism. Its adherents themselves usually present as conservative patriots and reject the label.
scope: The mainstream Italian strand: the MSI's transformation into Alleanza Nazionale at Fiuggi (1995) under Gianfranco Fini and its heir Brothers of Italy under Giorgia Meloni (2022 programme), read with Tamás's and Griffin's concept as summarised on Wikipedia. Fringe neo-fascist, neo-Nazi and paramilitary currents, and the Hungarian illiberal and Jobbik variants, are excluded except where noted.

keyFigures.name: Gianfranco Fini

keyFigures.name: Giorgia Meloni
keyFigures.role: Leader of Brothers of Italy, the post-fascist party that has led Italy's government since the 2022 election

keyFigures.name: Gáspár Miklós Tamás
keyFigures.role: Philosopher who first defined the term post-fascism

sources.usedFor: Fiuggi legacy, FdI's relation to its fascist past, Ignazi on continuity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The FdI programme keeps the national health service and pledges to strengthen it, as AN's statist right did; no push to dismantle public care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: the programme prefers tax relief and contract-based pay to statutory floors; it does not propose a minimum wage rise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Post-fascists back the market economy and deregulation yet remain more statist than Forza Italia and favour state protection of strategic sectors, so adherents split.

public-ownership.rationale: AN backed privatisation, though it kept a statist streak; the FdI programme does not call for nationalising utilities, only for strategic state oversight.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The FdI programme centres on lower taxes, flat-tax extensions and family quotients, not higher taxes on the rich.

unions-good.rationale: The social-right tradition valued labour dignity ("work expresses citizens' dignity" in the programme) but the right is wary of union politics; neither clear support nor opposition.

property-fundamental.rationale: The programme makes the family home unseizable and defends enterprise, treating property as a protected right, though not absolute against national interest.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The programme promises deregulation and simplification but also curbs on tax-haven relocation and unfair competition; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: It abolishes the citizenship income for able-bodied people yet expands family, pension and disability support, so it neither wants broad cuts nor an unconditional welfare state.

worker-ownership.rationale: Post-fascism sits comfortably in global capitalism and does not flirt with anti-capitalism (Tamás); worker ownership is not on its agenda.

surveillance-ok.rationale: AN stood for tough security and law-and-order measures; the programme backs more police powers, though it rejects mass digital control and social scoring.

legalize-drugs.rationale: AN prohibited all drugs including cannabis, and the programme vows to fight drug dealing and use "by every means".

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The programme stresses free expression against arbitrary social-media censorship, while demanding intransigence against antisemitism and racism; leans against speech laws.

strong-leader.rationale: The programme promotes presidentialism for stable governments with a direct link between citizens and leader, and Fiuggi evoked plebiscitary democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: A state-centred national right that wants an efficient, authoritative state; no source discusses anarchism.

limit-guns.rationale: The programme is silent on guns; Italy already has strict rules and adherents are not engaged on the question; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The programme explicitly calls for more staff, equipment and legal protection for police and armed forces, and AN stood for law and order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values stance attributed to AN, close to the Church.

decide-locally.rationale: AN long preferred presidentialism and a unitary national state, accepting federalism only later and with emphasis on national cohesion and unity.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme stresses certainty of punishment, against "empty-the-prisons" measures, with only a prison-building plan.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme calls the family the founding community of society and a "sacred good" to protect, not an outdated institution.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The programme keeps civil unions only and reaffirms the ban on adoption by same-sex couples, opposing marriage equality.

abortion-legal.rationale: The programme says to protect human life from its beginning while stopping short of repealing Law 194, so adherents lean against but accept it.

more-religion-public.rationale: Traditional values close to the Catholic Church, and the programme defends the Judeo-Christian roots of Europe.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not an Italian post-fascist theme; the right emphasises equal opportunity and anti-discrimination in general terms, not race-conscious remedies.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The programme defends the traditional family and rejects same-sex parenting, signalling opposition to constructivist gender claims; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: National identity, heritage and patriotism are at the centre of both AN's and FdI's self-description.

gradual-change.rationale: Post-fascists seek national regeneration and a constitutional overhaul (presidentialism) and break with the old party system, not cautious incrementalism, while working through institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The 2022 Brothers of Italy programme calls for stopping illegal immigration, a naval blockade of departures and limits on flows.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The programme favours a "Europe of the Fatherlands" and national interest in foreign policy, not stronger global bodies, though it backs NATO and the UN-era order.

free-trade.rationale: The programme stresses Made in Italy protection, short supply chains and fair-competition rules while promoting exports; adherents split.

nation-first.rationale: The programme frames foreign policy around "the protection of the national interest and the defence of the Fatherland".

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: It supports Western alliances and Ukraine's defence, but human-rights interventions are not a stated theme; adherents split.

open-borders.rationale: It demands border defence and control; open borders conflict with its identity politics.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme says environmental respect and growth are complementary, not opposed, and targets growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: It favours a "compatible development" and criticises costly green transition measures, rejecting drastic state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The programme backs innovation and digitalisation but offers no technological optimism as doctrine.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The programme stresses energy independence but nuclear power is not clearly addressed in the sections read; split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Post-fascism works without coups or revolution (Tamás), and Fiuggi accepted the democratic rules; only a radical rebirth rhetoric survives.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programme praises popular sovereignty and attacks palace governments and technocrats, favouring elected leaders.

central-planning.rationale: Post-fascism is at home in global capitalism and promotes enterprise; planned economy is rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a post-fascist position; they favour private enterprise and see workers' ownership as leftist.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not in the programme, which wants to cut taxes broadly and eliminate Irap; the proposal replaces most taxes, a notion foreign to it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The programme stresses protecting family wealth and the first home, so heavy inheritance taxes would be opposed.

basic-income.rationale: The programme abolishes the Citizenship Income and replaces it with aid only for those unable to work.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The programme stresses Made in Italy and fair competition but not tariff barriers within the EU; adherents split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: AN was more interventionist than other centre-right parties, and the programme favours state-guided strategic sectors and energy security.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme exalts SMEs, artisans, the self-employed and the family home as the backbone of Italian society.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Brothers of Italy accepts a market economy and the 2022 programme backs enterprise and work; it does not discuss abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The 2022 programme seeks changes to European rules and credit access, not the end of central banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The fascist corporatist heritage was dropped; the programme proposes market-oriented labour reforms and tax measures, not state bodies fixing wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Post-fascists compete in elections and accepted democracy at Fiuggi, dropping single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: MSI/AN accepted the Republic; the programme does not support restoring monarchy, though some tolerate it.

democracy-best.rationale: They accept electoral democracy as a vehicle while remaining sceptical of liberal democracy (Tamás), so agreement is real but qualified.

direct-votes.rationale: Plebiscitary democracy was a Fiuggi theme, yet the programme proposes direct election of the leader rather than referendums; split.

workers-councils.rationale: The strand works within parliamentary democracy and its programme proposes a presidential reform, not council power; no source discusses councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme talks of "national cohesion and unity"; secession is rejected, and AN opposed Lega's separatism.

natural-rulers.rationale: Tamás stresses rejection of universal citizenship, yet parties publicly claim democratic equality; adherents are split on innate rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Post-fascism avoids paramilitary violence (Tamás), but some members still tolerate or minimise neo-fascist violence, so agreement is moderate.

war-builds-character.rationale: They have dropped the fascist cult of war; the programme speaks of defence and alliances.

separate-church-state.rationale: Traditional values close to the Church and Judeo-Christian heritage claims make strict separation unlikely.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion is invoked as cultural heritage, but the programme upholds constitutional democracy rather than scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme strengthens public police, armed forces and courts; it does not discuss private provision.

military-superiority.rationale: It increases defence spending to NATO targets and calls for strong armed forces, though not explicit superiority over rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: They claim "French identity" or national identity protection; statements stress a culturally rather than racially defined nation, yet sympathy exists.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The strand stresses national solidarity over class conflict; no source discusses the Marxist theory of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The programme speaks of equal opportunity ("pari opportunità") and merit, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not an Italian issue; nationalism's emphasis on state sovereignty over territory implies opposition; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The programme stresses national pride and a Mattei-style cooperation with Africa, not reparations; inferred from its patriotic framing.

civilizational-union.rationale: It stresses Western and Judeo-Christian roots and a Europe of nations; a political union is not sought.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The programme values enterprise as a resource, but communal and national duty dominates over egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The Fiuggi theses evoke an ethical state and national community and the programme speaks of the Fatherland to love and defend.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The programme treats natural resources as heritage to preserve yet argues for growth; no intrinsic-value doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: The programme's first priority is raising the birth rate with family support.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme champions industry, enterprise and Made in Italy as sources of national growth, so it treats industrial society as an achievement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: It values innovation but would protect institutions and tradition against disruption.

human-enhancement.rationale: Traditional-values right, with bioethical conservatism (opposing surrogacy); transhumanist freedoms are unlikely; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The programme rejects mass digital control and scoring and wants elected leaders.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Adherents balance privacy protection against a security stance; not addressed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Griffin describes post-fascist rhetoric as national rebirth of a fallen nation, with traditional-value restoration, but the stress is on regeneration in modern form.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The programme says freedom and rights outweigh "ideological visions", a pragmatic phrase, yet it is itself ideologically distinct.

direct-action.rationale: Post-fascists pursue change by elections and institutions, rejecting extra-parliamentary action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nothing in post-fascist sources addresses whether means must mirror ends; adherents pursue nationalist aims through ordinary electoral politics, so no lean is inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a programme built on growth, industry and modern state capacity.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a pro-enterprise, pro-work programme that values trades, artisans and professions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The programme rewards work and enterprise within a market economy; distribution by need is not discussed.

production-for-use.rationale: The 2022 programme treats profit-making firms as a resource for the nation; production for use is not discussed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The programme says those who create wealth are a resource, "not an enemy".

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Anti-communism is one of the traits post-fascists retain from fascism, so a class dictatorship is rejected outright.

collective-farming.rationale: Anti-communist and committed to small owners, artisans and family property, post-fascism opposes collectivised agriculture.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The strand treats capitalism as compatible with the national interest; no source discusses the theory of imperialism.

taxation-theft.rationale: It wants lower taxes and calls the burden "asphyxiating", but supports the state and its revenue.

harm-principle.rationale: Traditional values and security positions justify restricting conduct beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Post-fascism prioritises nation and community, with Tamás noting a break with universal individual citizenship.

conscription.rationale: The programme upholds armed forces staffing and civic service for youth; conscription is not proposed, adherents are split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme stresses popular sovereignty, voting legitimacy and love of the homeland, which makes emigration a poor substitute for the vote.

state-as-business.rationale: The programme wants an efficient administration but the state remains a national authority, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: AN's social right and the programme's welfare for families and the vulnerable coexist with free enterprise stress; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: The right accuses the left of dominating institutions and complains about social-media censorship; inferred for the elite-critical line.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Modern post-fascists have disowned biological racism (Fini on 1938 racial laws), though fringes persist.

organic-representation.rationale: AN and FdI accepted party-based parliamentary democracy, with presidentialism, rather than corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: Post-fascism is explicitly non-totalitarian; the programme complains the state is too invasive.

national-rebirth.rationale: Contested: Griffin's palingenesis defines fascism, and post-fascism is the move away from it, but the 2022 programme speaks of raising Italy from decline and Ignazi reads the strand as continuous with the MSI.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a theme in AN or FdI, which accept existing borders and alliances, while Jobbik-type irredentism is a fringe strand.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A feudal idea never raised; post-fascists rest authority on elections and constitutional offices.

bound-labor.rationale: A feudal idea never raised; the programme speaks of dignified work as a citizen's right.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed by post-fascist sources; the right criticises left dominance of institutions but does not endorse a power-knowledge thesis.

universal-morality.rationale: They invoke Judeo-Christian and classical roots and values like liberty and justice; a mild yes inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Some national-unity thinking, but they compete in a pluralist party system.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: AN supported Israel and sought better relations with Jewish groups.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The programme encourages the return of Italians abroad and people of Italian descent.

revive-national-language.rationale: No stated position; Italian is not a dormant language, so the issue does not arise.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The programme speaks of dignified work but not co-determination.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme backs parity schools and school choice for families; inferred moderate support.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The programme seeks a revision of EU stability rules for growth, while preaching sound public accounts; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: It speaks of fiscal liberty and entrepreneurship, but not as a doctrinal precondition.

rule-by-example.rationale: The programme relies on police powers, tougher penalties and legal order, not mainly on rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Post-fascist neo-nationalism endorses national sovereignty and a nation-state, with its own people's priority.

force-without-un.rationale: The programme stresses NATO and allied action but says nothing on Security Council approval; inferred as split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Appeals to Catholic and traditional values and national sentiment make a "reason only" claim unlikely.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Post-fascism strips immigrants of full citizenship rights (Stanley-Becker), and the right favours priority for nationals.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The programme abolishes unconditional income support for the able-bodied and pushes job-linked aid.

class-collaboration.rationale: Fascist heritage of national solidarity above class conflict carried on in the social-right and in the programme's pro-enterprise, pro-work message.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The programme calls the nation's natural and artistic heritage an inheritance to guard and develop, the opposite of sacrificing it.

dominated-front.rationale: Meloni-style post-fascists place Italy firmly in the Western camp ("a natural choice, not a political calculation"), not in a bloc against it.

workers-nation.rationale: National solidarity and patriotism outrank internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme advocates female equality, pink tax removal and a glass-ceiling break while defending the traditional family; split.

ban-interest.rationale: The programme wants better access to credit for firms and savers and treats banks as engines of development.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Mainstream post-fascists disavow racial laws, which Fini called infamous.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis; post-fascism is anti-communist and presents the state as a national, not class, authority.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme backs energy independence including gas production.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The RN and others speak of protecting national identity; the programme also favours inclusion of regular migrants.

elite-replacement.rationale: The idea does not appear in the sources read for AN or FdI, which stress immigration control and identity but not a deliberate replacement plot; adherents are split and no lean is inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: AN long favoured plurality voting and presidentialism to secure stable governments.

national-mission.rationale: Not a theme; modern post-fascists reject missionary universalism in favour of "Europe of nations".

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The programme counters stereotypes but does not frame society as systemically male-advantaging.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme blames a political class that abandoned the national interest, and Fiuggi capitalised on Tangentopoli.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Post-fascists repudiated the fascist past and the Catholic-leaning right opposes eugenics; no source discusses it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The right defends security forces and gives them legal protection.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They support an active state in the economy, culture and security.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: AN leaders repudiated fascist racial laws; Fini called the 1938 laws infamous, so discouraging mixed marriage is disowned.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Fini and others accept the democratic equality of persons formally and condemn discrimination, yet Tamás argues they reject universal citizenship.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Anti-communism leaves no room for a socialist debate; post-fascists oppose socialism wherever it is built.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: AN supported Israel and sought better ties with Jewish groups, so it rejects the colonial characterisation.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist stress on common national law and cohesion; not directly stated.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from a constitutional, liberal-democratic framework that protects freedom of belief.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: An issue foreign to European post-fascism; inferred from its pro-farming, pro-enterprise stance.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The programme backs parity schools and humanist-Christian roots.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The programme invokes "sovereignty belongs to the people" and electoral legitimacy.

trade-surplus.rationale: The programme promotes exports and Made in Italy but never makes a surplus a goal, so adherents are unlikely to take a side.

population-transfer.rationale: Mainstream parties avoid it, but expulsion of irregular migrants is pushed; for minorities that are citizens it is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Post-fascists back state force through police, army and punishment, so an absolute ban on initiating force is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Fascist social-Darwinian heritage dropped, while market competition is endorsed; split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Post-fascists were themselves once outside the constitutional arc and their programme is silent on banning parties, while anti-communism pulls toward yes; inferred as split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican-theory idea absent from post-fascist sources; no lean is inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The programme seeks a strong directly elected executive and judicial reform (separate careers for prosecutors and judges), mixing checks with executive stability; split.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine; post-fascists are anti-communist and compete in elections.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The programme gives priority to families and workers rather than the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Pro-home-ownership but not specifically British council housing; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: AN's law-and-order stance suggests support for restrictions; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The programme blames decline on political choices and treats a low birth rate as the problem, not excess population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Sweden Democrats seek abolition of multiculturalism and the RN defends identity, implying diversity strains cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rejects lotteries; however, the programme proposes lottery selection for CSM judicial council members only.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Law-and-order instincts pull toward yes, but the programme also pledges respect for constitutional freedoms; inferred as split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: AN was more interventionist than other centre-right parties, but its market commitments cut against price fixing; split.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme opposes censorship and defends free expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: The programme places the armed forces under the state and the nation, and wants a directly elected president, not a party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hard-line immigration and citizenship restrictions in the RN and others.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; anti-elite rhetoric suggests sympathy but the programme proposes no pay cap.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Leader-centred parties enforce cohesion, but no doctrine of binding decisions is stated; inferred as neutral.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Calls for "Europe of the Fatherlands", not pooling sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The programme's presidentialism implies a strong executive head.

church-by-bishops.rationale: An internal church-governance question that post-fascist sources never address.

clerical-rule.rationale: The programme works within a constitutional republic and cites Judeo-Christian heritage as culture, not clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Patriotic loyalty is central; "defending the Fatherland" is a stated duty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The programme stresses free expression, though traditionalists back moral limits.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The programme proposes presidentialism without stating term limits, so no lean is inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Not addressed; the programme prefers stable executives, which cuts against recall, while populism favours it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme demands full respect of alliances, higher NATO-level defence spending and Italy as NATO founder member.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a market-friendly programme that defends property rights.

people-in-arms.rationale: The programme strengthens the professional armed forces and promotes military academies.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; the programme celebrates mountain and island specificities and agriculture but not the moral superiority of rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Jobbik-type irredentism is fringe; mainstream post-fascists do not push it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from anti-elite, populist rhetoric against a ruling class said to be removed from ordinary Italians; not stated about graduates.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They defend Western and Judeo-Christian roots as particular; not cultural relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: AN positions were not uniform; hardliners favoured it, others disagreed; split.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The programme stresses parental priority and traditional values.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; the programme backs school quality and research, and Italy's right has not made creationism an issue.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-values stance attributed to AN, close to the Catholic Church.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Its programme welcomes return of oriundi and the RN/others favour blood links.

minority-language-support.rationale: The programme values local specificities but stresses national unity; no stated line.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from an emphasis on common national law and cohesion; not addressed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred: national tradition and identity are prized over non-conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The programme stresses sound public finances and creditor credibility for Italy; cancellation is not discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A decolonisation-era question; post-fascists accept the existing economic system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The programme reforms the constitution through the parliament and presidentialism.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The programme says rights and freedoms prevail over ideological visions and promises democratic safeguards.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: A "Mattei formula for Africa" of cooperation exists, but not a duty to the world's poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Italy relies on NATO's protection and the programme backs alliances; own deterrent not discussed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Presidentialism is the programme's flagship institutional reform, for a direct link between citizens and the leader; AN backed it for decades.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The programme asks to revise EU economic governance but does not address central-bank independence.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed in sources on the issue; supporters of Israel could go either way.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Inferred from a social-right tradition and a programme that ties enterprise and family property to national interest.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; anti-communists see the USSR as totalitarian.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The programme argues environment and growth are compatible and favours "compatible development" over restrictive precaution.

collective-defense.rationale: The programme calls NATO membership a natural choice and demands full respect of alliances.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The programme supports Ukraine against Russia's aggression, implying unlawful annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Traditional-values stance close to the Church and Judeo-Christian heritage claims.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The programme wants a directly elected political leader heading the government, not a figurehead above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: AN stressed national cohesion and opposed Lega separatism; the programme ties federalism to "cohesion and national unity".

region-keeps-system.rationale: Fiscal federalism and autonomies are supported within national unity; not addressed for a distinct system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divine-ruler idea never raised; the programme rests on popular sovereignty.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The programme extends flat taxes for the self-employed and on income increases, with a view to wider flat taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; the programme stresses family and education as formative but takes no stance.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The programme speaks of rights and constitutional principles.

space-expansion.rationale: The programme mentions a national space policy but not a civilisational goal.

leader-cult.rationale: Fini and AN distanced themselves from Mussolini; leader prominence persists (La Russa busts).

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-centred, but silent on custody rules.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate; post-fascists are anti-communist.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme defends property and the small owner and rejects expropriation.

refugee-return.rationale: The programme filters asylum seekers and prioritises return of irregulars.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: AN and FdI accept existing borders; Jobbik-style irredentism is a fringe exception noted in the sources.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred: a constitutional democracy party that protects freedoms; the issue is alien to its framework.

women-must-cover.rationale: The Sweden Democrats propose banning Islamic dress, and so some would restrict covering, not require it.

common-currency.rationale: The programme works within the euro and EU institutions but wants a "Europe of the Fatherlands"; adherents split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not a post-fascist theme; Europe is imagined as a union of nations, not a merger of kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from unitary-nationalist emphasis on national cohesion over minority self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; sources mention support for Israel but no stated view on diaspora strategy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: A Marxist doctrine; post-fascists stress nation, identity and will.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme mentions countering unfair competition and tax-haven avoidance but not antitrust.

no-bailouts.rationale: The programme backs savers' protection and credit support, but a general no-bailout line is not stated.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Tamás reports Orbán saying elections would not remove him and the programme stresses popular sovereignty and attacks palace governments; sources show majoritarian instincts but contested among adherents.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The programme promotes equal opportunity and breaking the glass ceiling, but not mandatory parity quotas.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme stresses exports, internationalisation and Europe, not a closed bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: The programme favours fair competition rules, but binding trade-treaty standards are not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: The programme rewards enterprise and profits; moral incentives are not discussed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Post-fascism works without coups or paramilitary violence (Tamás, Stanley-Becker).

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Italy has no titles in law, so the issue is dormant.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The programme stresses cultural identity, classical and Judeo-Christian roots and national heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Not addressed; the programme's Africa policy speaks of respect for peoples and cooperation.

patriotic-education.rationale: The programme speaks of love of the Fatherland and patriotic commitment; AN stressed patriotism and national identity.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from the stress on equal opportunity and merit and the absence of race-conscious remedies.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; the programme seeks to revise EU rules, not to nationalise money creation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Tamás says post-fascism fits comfortably in global capitalism and does not flirt with anti-capitalism.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The programme promotes a Mediterranean and African "Mattei" model, but not framed as imperial influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme promotes exports and internationalisation of Italian firms.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory; post-fascists reject it as part of their anti-communism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The programme pledges to fight discrimination and demands intransigence against racism and antisemitism.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The programme affirms constitutional freedoms but proposes institutional change; no stance on entrenchment.

elective-rulers.rationale: The programme stresses popular sovereignty and a directly elected leader.

minority-veto.rationale: Contrary to the majority-driven stability the programme seeks.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The presidentialist programme shifts power from parliament to a directly elected leader.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as the common conservative position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from the social-right tradition that stresses national solidarity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Post-fascists are committed activists who stress patriotic engagement and mobilisation.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine; post-fascism is anti-communist and rejects socialist state-building.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The Fiuggi theses call antifascism a necessary historical moment but not a self-standing founding value, a stance the party took to end its isolation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Fiuggi put fascism, Nazism and communism under the single category of totalitarianism and rejected communist-style antifascism.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: post-fascist parties object to liberal cultural elites rather than to mass culture as a tool of pacification.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the strand does not use a theory of cultural hegemony; it casts itself as the voice of the people against elites.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Tamas stresses that post-fascism fits easily into global capitalism, and the FdI programme accepts the market economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: the parties are restrictionist on immigration but operate within EU and democratic citizenship rules, with no stated rule reserving offices for native-born citizens.

party-own-road.rationale: Not a post-fascist concern, as these parties are anti-communist and not part of communist networks; inferred as neutral.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from sovereigntist, national-interest positions; the FdI programme also stays within NATO and the EU, so it is only a mild lean.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: AN and FdI accepted the postwar borders at Fiuggi and in government, though the Istrian exile cause remains symbolically important.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the strand's ultranationalism puts the existing national majority first and rejects group-based political privilege for pre-colonial descendants.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical question outside the strand's concerns; inferred as neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from a patriotic politics of national heritage and opposition to what it calls cancel culture; not stated in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a defining issue; the FdI programme stresses family and natality, so adherents are neutral on this.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not a defining issue; inferred as neutral.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its civilisational nationalism and scepticism of liberal universalism (s1); the parties still work within Western democratic institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The strand dropped totalitarian methods and works within electoral democracy; the FdI programme seeks presidentialism, not a political role for the army.

paid-care-work.rationale: The FdI programme emphasises family support and measures for mothers and births, which is consistent with recognising care work, though not framed as wages for housework.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the Brothers of Italy programme's emphasis on the family and traditional values.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the party works within electoral democracy and favours presidentialism, with no push for examination-based office.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The programme defends national strategic interests and industries, in line with its nation-first stance.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family values, though it has not sought to repeal Italian divorce law.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: the programme seeks a stronger executive through presidentialism, not binding delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred: the programme keeps a statist, welfare-friendly pension system and does not push privatisation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from its strong defence of private property and rejection of land redistribution.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: As a party working within electoral democracy, post-fascism accepts parliamentary control of the budget.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from its nationalism and stress on assimilating immigrants into Italian culture.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the programme backs capitalist property rights, though its nation-first stance tempers this.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: It rejects equal outcomes and opposes treating group disparities as discrimination.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Tamas stresses that post-fascism fits easily into global capitalism, so it has no anti-consumerist programme.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from its NATO alignment and stress on order and security over support for rebels.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from its strong support for collective defence by consent within NATO and the EU, not forced membership.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred: Tamás stresses post-fascism fits easily into global capitalism, and the FdI programme does not attack lobbying; adherents split between populist anti-elite rhetoric and business ties.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Post-fascist parties frame NGOs and foreign money as threats to national sovereignty; the FdI programme defends national interest against outside influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The FdI programme pairs family support and birth-rate incentives with opposition to mass immigration as the answer to demographic decline.

residents-only-property.rationale: Inferred: the sources record no position on local property purchase limits; nationalist localism and the party's pro-property stance pull in opposite directions.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: the programme favours tax relief and private enterprise over state employment schemes, so a public job guarantee is unlikely to be endorsed.

democratic-peace.rationale: Inferred from ultranationalism and hostility to liberal universalism: adherents distrust democracy promotion as a liberal-internationalist project.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Post-fascists stress state authority, law and order and tough security, so a general right to disobey runs against their core stance.

non-intervention.rationale: Inferred: the party backs sovereignty but also NATO and a role for Italy abroad, so it would not accept an absolute ban on intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Inferred: AN and FdI abandoned corporatist economics and the statist class-collaboration model, and the sources show no push for industry-wide unions.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Inferred: scholars note the shift away from open conspiracism towards conservative-patriot framing, so mainstream post-fascists publicly reject such claims though fringes keep them.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The FdI programme stresses the traditional family founded on marriage, so abolishing legal marriage runs against its core family values.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred: the sources do not address freedom-of-information law; the programme speaks of transparency while the strong-state tradition favours executive discretion.

local-production.rationale: Inferred: the FdI programme defends Italian farming and made-in-Italy production as a national-interest policy.

informal-organisation.rationale: Post-fascists keep permanent parties and strong leadership structures, as the AN and FdI party organisations show.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The FdI programme asserts national sovereignty and constitutional primacy against EU and supranational bodies, though it stays in NATO.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred: Catholic identity features in the rhetoric of Italian post-fascists, but the nation is defined mainly by ethnicity and culture and adherents split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: post-fascists stress national sovereignty and Atlanticist alliances, and nothing in the FdI programme supports tributary deference to another power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred: Brothers of Italy backs fiscal federalism and differentiated autonomy only as a coalition compromise, while the national-unity tradition of AN resists regional retention; adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: the statement presupposes common ownership of the means of production, which post-fascists reject, so the pairing is not one they would endorse.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism is a core feature of post-fascist parties, and the Fiuggi theses condemned communism together with fascism as totalitarianism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: the FdI programme favours a market economy with freedom of choice in services alongside a strengthened public health service.

religion-illusion.rationale: Inferred: the movement champions traditional Catholic identity and Christian roots, so it would not call religion an illusion, though it is mainly a cultural rather than doctrinal stance.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred: post-fascists accept the market economy and, per Tamas, fit easily into global capitalism; a historical-progress framing is not documented, hence low confidence.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: the family-centred programme sees women reconciling work and family through tax relief and incentives, not through economic-system transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: The FdI programme centres the natural family and supports it through incentives and bonuses, which rules out socialising housework and childcare.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: AN and FdI defend Italian language and culture but the programme does not call for purging loanwords; adherents are split, as the fascist-era campaign was not revived.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: the question of treaties with internal nations has not been addressed by post-fascists; their national-unity stance is neither clearly for nor against.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Post-fascism is ultranationalist and state-centred, and its programme has no place for property-holding cooperative communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: the nationalist right opposes a minority-majority framing but state-sponsored settlement of the majority group is not part of the documented programme.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Inferred: post-fascists reject communism and, having dropped corporatism, accept capitalism; yet some rhetoric about a national third way persists, so adherents are split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist emphasis on national identity and homeland; documents do not state a view on competing claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Alleanza Nazionale at Fiuggi renounced fascism and condemned the racial laws, and Meloni's party rejects denialism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The party defends traditional family values but accepts that homosexuality is legal, and it does not propose criminalising it.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Post-fascism is defined by working within electoral democracy and dropping authoritarian methods.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The parties invoke Christian identity but operate within a secular constitution and do not seek blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred: not a theme of modern post-fascist programmes, which have dropped the imperial project.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic-law question outside the ideology's concerns.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the parties accept electoral legitimacy and oppose Islamist armed movements.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme emphasises strong government and direct presidential election rather than workplace or community self-management.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: The programme rejects identity-based oppression frameworks as divisive ideology.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The Brothers of Italy programme defends the traditional family and opposes gender-identity measures.

assisted-dying.rationale: The party's Catholic-influenced defence of life makes it opposed to assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fiuggi positioned AN firmly on the national right, though it also claimed to go beyond old ideological divides; most adherents keep the right label.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; post-fascists accept capitalism and stress national solidarity over class.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The programme stresses defence of Western Christian identity and opposes Islamist influence, and the wider family treats Islam as a cultural challenge.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Invokes God and Christian roots in its slogan but grounds authority in popular sovereignty and the constitution.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Mixed: defence of Christian symbols such as the crucifix coexists with hostility to Islamic dress, so no single position.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A labour-law detail the programme does not address.

social-market-economy.rationale: The programme favours a market economy with state support for families, workers and strategic sectors.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The programme calls for strong armed forces and security, and the tradition prizes the military.

rich-first.rationale: The programme has no stated view on staged enrichment; neutral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme commits Italy to NATO and the Atlantic alliance.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Post-fascist parties work within electoral democracy and select leaders by party vote; hereditary leadership is foreign to them.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: they accept global capitalism and ordinary banking, having dropped corporatist economics.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: Brothers of Italy has criticised EU constraints rhetorically but governed within EU fiscal rules, so adherents are split.

property-franchise.rationale: These parties compete in universal-suffrage elections and the Fiuggi turn accepted liberal democracy.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: the traditional-family emphasis is opposed to ecofeminist critiques of domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred: they accept global capitalism and reject Marxist critique of it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: they defend formal press and assembly freedoms within a market economy, though they criticise media bias.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Having accepted liberal democratic constitutionalism at Fiuggi, they work under standing laws, though they favour strong executive and security powers.

racial-franchise.rationale: Post-fascists work within electoral democracy and officially reject racial exclusion from the franchise, which is a fringe neo-fascist stance.

online-participation.rationale: Never a stated plank; adherents are indifferent.

open-government-data.rationale: Never a stated plank; no basis to infer a position.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred: they stress Catholic identity but do not seek legal limits on interfaith marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Parties seeking respectability in electoral democracy disown such discrimination, which belongs to the fringe currents the scope excludes.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the FdI programme favours elected, strong government and direct presidential-style legitimacy, not sortition; the issue is not addressed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: the programme defends Christian roots and traditional values as national heritage, favouring preservation over reform of doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Inferred: Tamás stresses that post-fascism sits easily with global capitalism, and the FdI programme stresses enterprise rather than limits on wealth.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-family stance of AN and Brothers of Italy; Italy permits open service, and the parties have not campaigned against it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The movement defends Christian and national tradition, and the FdI programme invokes Italy's Christian identity.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The FdI programme calls for tougher security, more police and certain punishment.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the movement's ultranationalism and its preference for a unitary national community over group-based power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred as split: the parties back family-based and subsidiarity-style welfare but keep the state health and pension systems.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the parties favour strong, stable executives such as direct election of the premier and have no stated term-limit plank.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the movement's preference for strong representative leadership; direct and liquid democracy are not part of its programme.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from a programme centred on national interest, security and demography rather than global catastrophic risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's alignment with traditional Catholic and family values.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: Italian law already makes spouses equal, and the movement stresses the traditional family without demanding husbandly authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to immigration and ultranationalism; it offers no local voting rights to foreign residents.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from its market-friendly, pro-property conservatism; rent caps are not part of the FdI programme.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from Tamas's point that post-fascism fits easily into global capitalism, which relies on strong intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Post-fascism drops paramilitary methods and mass-movement drill in favour of electoral democracy, as AN's Fiuggi turn did.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from the Italian right's Atlanticism and NATO membership; it has not campaigned to remove allied nuclear weapons.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from AN's and FdI's Atlanticist, NATO-aligned stance; allied bases are accepted.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist right's readiness to commemorate its own nation's victims and recognised atrocities; the sources do not address genocide recognition directly.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The ideology's sources do not address this; it mixes defence of work and family with a pro-property, capitalist outlook.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Post-fascist parties keep tough security policies and ultranationalism, so absolute pacifism contradicts their stance.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Griffin sees post-fascism as a nationalist rebirth project, which stresses continuity of the nation from its origins.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The FdI programme defends the traditional family and opposes what it calls gender ideology.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from its traditional family values and rejection of liberal universalism; feminist theory is not engaged directly.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist tradition of honouring those who died for Italy; the sources do not discuss martyr language directly.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Mainstream post-fascists present as conservative patriots and stress 'God, homeland, family' themes, but do not frame politics as a cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from ultranationalism, which seeks to unite the nation in its own state rather than treat the homeland as a diaspora centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Rebirth nationalism stresses cultural renewal, but the electoral parties pursue state power at the same time.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from its traditional, Catholic-leaning conservatism, which keeps conventional religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from traditional family values; feminist tests of scripture are not part of the programme.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Post-fascism has dropped corporatist economics for capitalism yet keeps 'Italians first' priorities on welfare and work; adherents are mixed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from its ultranationalist preference for strong central states; the sources do not address it.

independent-unions.rationale: Post-fascist parties work within democracy and accept unions, but no source states a position on their independence.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from post-fascism's anti-communism and fit with capitalism, which rejects working-class rule as a test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Post-fascist programmes do not make a distinct case on local public services; adherents are split.

second-chamber.rationale: Italy's post-fascists work within a two-chamber parliament and have no stated line on the structure.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the strong view of property and the rejection of worker ownership in other answers.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from the unitary, nationalist outlook, which opposes devolving decisions to local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: The 2022 programme stresses support for families and births; a family wage is inferred from that.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug approval is not addressed in the sources.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research is not addressed in the sources.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the party's tough security stance and acceptance of surveillance.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the tough security stance, which favours identifiability over anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: Post-fascism mixes strong-state nationalism with acceptance of liberal democracy, so adherents are split.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the traditional values and religion-friendly family outlook of post-fascist parties.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Post-fascists want a strong central state but have accepted regional autonomy as a compromise; split.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the protective, tradition-minded stance on food and farming; not documented in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form is not addressed in the sources.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Post-fascist parties usually reject the racial label and present as patriots, though they favour the national majority; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride is framed as national and cultural rather than racial, and adherents avoid racial claims; split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred from the Fiuggi turn to democratic politics and NATO membership, though ultranationalism leaves room for assertiveness.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The Fiuggi turn dropped irredentist claims; Italian post-fascists define the nation by culture and history within the state, so cross-border language claims are not a plank.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from its civic-national stance within electoral democracy and its hostility to communal or multicultural arrangements.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The FdI programme is sovereigntist and wary of Brussels, but it does not claim outside powers are plotting to break up Italy.

free-public-college.rationale: The programme prioritises tax cuts and merit, with no pledge of free tuition; inferred from that.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from the FdI programme's scepticism toward costly green policies and its pro-business, tax-cutting line.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the programme's emphasis on the family, birth rate and national patrimony passed on to the young.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The programme stresses family and motherhood and also promotes women's careers; adherents do not clearly claim distinct female values deserve more weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from its NATO-aligned stance and pledges to strengthen national defence and security.

open-diplomacy.rationale: No source states a view on secret treaties; inferred neutral given an Atlanticist right that accepts normal confidential diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Per Tamas, post-fascism fits easily into global capitalism, and the FdI programme accepts the EU single market; inferred from that.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Post-fascist parties dropped paramilitary violence and work within electoral democracy, and stress a tough, state-led security order.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from strong nationalism, respect for the armed forces and Atlanticism in the Brothers of Italy programme.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Alleanza Nazionale and Brothers of Italy gave no clear position on bargaining; the right is split between social and market-oriented views.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the programme's emphasis on supporting families and workers' incomes, though tax credits are not named.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Brothers of Italy criticise EU fiscal rules while governing under them, so adherents are split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from the programme's national-interest, sovereignty-first outlook toward international institutions.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Post-fascism is defined by its turn to electoral democracy and the institutional state, rejecting revolutionary overthrow.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the programme's statist, national-interest economics, which favours Italian policy over experiments.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Never addressed as a core position; the programme mentions the environment without a stand on natural capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Ultranationalism and a national rebirth are core to the concept, and the programme centres the Italian nation and its identity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the fiscal caution and benefit-for-natives emphasis of the programme.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from the party's defence of a unified nation against regional and class framings.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the programme's traditionalist 'natural family' and Christian-identity language, which treats human nature as given.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from the right's push to shape the state broadcaster rather than defend its independence.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from the movement's defence of national Christian identity and tradition; it does not endorse religious universalism.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Brothers of Italy programme calls agriculture a pillar of the nation and promises supply-chain contracts that narrow the gap between production cost and sale price.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from its Atlanticism and commitment to NATO commitments; the programme does not discuss nuclear weapons.

workers-own-party.rationale: Post-fascist parties present as broad national parties and dropped corporatism, so a separate workers' party runs against their cross-class pitch; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from its socially conservative, security-minded and anti-multicultural stance; not addressed in the sources.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property rights are uncontroversial in Italian law and the parties keep to it; the sources do not discuss it.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from its unitary nationalism, which stresses Italian language and 'italianità'; regional naming is not discussed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from the programme's reliance on public regulation and state planning for the environment.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from a parliamentary-democratic framework with no place for traditional leaders.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The programme says freedom and personal rights prevail over any ideology and that environment and growth are complementary.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The programme demands 'certezza della pena' and no early-release measures, which fits fixed sentences but does not state them.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from its hostility to immigration and defence of national identity; the programme stresses 'italianità'.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred: the Italian post-fascist right has not made union membership rules a distinct issue, so adherents are not clearly for or against.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the programme's emphasis on security, borders and national identity.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred: the Fratelli d'Italia programme defends the country's Christian identity and traditions, which sits against equal legal standing for all interpretations.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Fiuggi committed Alleanza Nazionale to electoral democracy and pluralism, and Brothers of Italy governs through elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred: despite the stress on traditional family, these parties do not seek to regulate private sexual conduct in a secular Italy.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred: parties that work inside electoral democracy and reject authoritarian methods do not advocate shutdowns.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred: the programme prefers family support and tax relief to replacing welfare with a single cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Post-fascist parties accept universal suffrage and have a woman prime minister, with no move to restrict women's political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The programme defends Christian and traditional-family identity and does not treat religion as a cause of women's oppression.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred: Fiuggi disowned racial laws, but the movement's cultural nationalism does not endorse the view that race is purely constructed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred: the programme backs family and equal-opportunity policy through government bodies, though it does not stress gender equality agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the FdI programme or Fiuggi theses; the statist, nationalist right has no stated theory of original appropriation.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from its sovereigntist stance and the programme's priority for national law over supranational bodies; no explicit position on criminal courts.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The programme invokes Christian identity but says nothing about literal scripture; adherents are not doctrinal on it.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the traditional-family emphasis in the programme; nothing on group self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Post-fascists dropped corporatism and work within global capitalism; defending a planned economy is alien, and the anti-communist heritage runs against it.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred from its push for direct election of the head of state (presidentialism) in the FdI programme.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred from the party's emphasis on Catholic and Christian national identity; the programme does not state a legal privilege.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Post-fascist parties stress a unitary nation-state and national identity, and oppose ethnic autonomy within the state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: nationalists in this strand split between self-determination and historical-claim arguments, and sources do not state a view.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not a stated issue for the Italian post-fascist strand; the question is anachronistic for it.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from its alignment with growth, consumption and global capitalism, as Tamas describes post-fascism.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from its unitary national identity and rejection of group-based rights.

equal-conscription.rationale: The programme stresses family and security but states no position on women in a draft; Italy has no conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Post-fascist parties keep ultranationalism and patriotic duty to the fatherland as core themes.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: These parties work within electoral democracy and the rule of law and dropped paramilitary violence.

close-ties-china.rationale: The governing FdI programme is Atlanticist, committed to NATO and the Western alliance.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Italian post-fascist concern for Italian communities abroad; not documented in the opened sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of capitalism and private property; not discussed.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from its rejection of liberal universalism in favour of nation, family and tradition.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the FdI programme's pro-tax-cut, pro-business stance; no specific plank checked.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from its statist, family-centred welfare orientation; not stated.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Post-fascists have accepted multiparty electoral democracy, so parties are not bypassed, though the FdI favours presidentialism.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from its populist anti-establishment rhetoric; not stated as a plank.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from Fratelli d'Italia's 'God, fatherland, family' identity and Christian-identity politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its modernised nationalist rebirth project combining modern capitalism with tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Divorce is legal in Italy and these parties do not seek to repeal it; inferred.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from its economic nationalism and defence of strategic national assets.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of capitalism and conservative-liberal economics; the sources do not discuss theories of just distribution.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of global capitalism (Tamas) and market-friendly programme; no source mentions this tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from its presentation as conservative patriots who reject charges of racism and stress other social causes; no source addresses the question directly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from its acceptance of electoral democracy and the rule of law and its emphasis on order and security.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on work, family and national production; the sources do not discuss automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Adherents are split: Brothers of Italy backs the Atlantic alliance while stressing a Europe of sovereign nations, so the sources do not give one answer.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Post-fascism dropped corporatist economics and fits easily into global capitalism, per Tamas, so it does not rest on labour as the source of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Its programme joins love of nation with social protection for Italian families and workers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from its priority on national identity, family and security over class politics; the question is about the left and is only loosely applicable.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anti-communism is a defining trait of the post-fascist tradition, so a communist-led market economy would be rejected.

missingStatements.text: Anti-fascism should be regarded as a founding value of a democratic constitution.
missingStatements.rationale: The Fiuggi theses call antifascism a necessary historical moment but not a self-standing founding value, a stance the party took to end its isolation.

missingStatements.text: Fascism and communism should be condemned together as equivalent forms of totalitarianism.
missingStatements.rationale: Fiuggi put fascism, Nazism and communism under the single category of totalitarianism and rejected communist-style antifascism.

notes: Contested: scholars such as Ignazi argue continuity with the MSI prevails in leadership and ideology, and Tamás treats post-fascism as a form of democratic fascism; adherents deny this. The Hungarian (Fidesz), French (RN) and Swedish variants would answer differently on the EU, Russia and welfare. Many answers are inferred because the parties' documents are silent on theoretical questions.
